'''Lawrence Sirovich''' is mathematical scientist whose research includes, among other topics, [[applied mathematics]], [[neuroscience]] and [[physics]]. He is recognized as the pioneer behind modern [[face recognition]], and is known for [[eigenfaces]], the method of snapshots, low dimensional dynamical systems, analysis of the [[Supreme Court of the United States|US Supreme Court]], neuronal population dynamics, and the faithful copy neuron.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.facefirst.com/blog/brief-history-of-face-recognition-software/|title=History of Face Recognition & Facial recognition software|date=2017-08-01|website=FaceFirst Face Recognition Software|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-25|archive-date=2021-04-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419163936/https://www.facefirst.com/blog/brief-history-of-face-recognition-software/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kirby|first1=M.|last2=Sirovich|first2=L.|date=1990|title=Application of the Karhunen-Loeve procedure for the characterization of human faces|journal=IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence|volume=12|issue=1|pages=103–108|doi=10.1109/34.41390|s2cid=570648|issn=0162-8828}}</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Sirovich|first=Lawrence|date=1987-10-01|title=Turbulence and the dynamics of coherent structures. II. Symmetries and transformations|journal=Quarterly of Applied Mathematics|volume=45|issue=3|pages=573–582|doi=10.1090/qam/910463|issn=0033-569X|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Omurtag|first1=A.|last2=Knight|first2=B. W.|last3=Sirovich|first3=L.|date=2000|title=Dynamics of Neuronal Populations: The Equilibrium Solution|journal=SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics|volume=60|issue=6|pages=2009–2028|doi=10.1137/s0036139998344921|s2cid=17760107|issn=0036-1399}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sirovich|first=Lawrence|date=2012-01-11|title=The faithful copy neuron|journal=Journal of Computational Neuroscience|volume=32|issue=3|pages=377–385|doi=10.1007/s10827-011-0356-6|pmid=22234837|s2cid=8404818|issn=0929-5313}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Sirovich was born to Jewish immigrants from Poland and raised in [[Brownsville, Brooklyn|Brownsville]], a working-class immigrant neighborhood of [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn, New York]]. He gained entrance to the [[Brooklyn Technical High School|Brooklyn Technical H.S.]], an experience which first opened his eyes to the possibilities of the world. There he was captain of the math team and years later, in 2018, inducted into the BTHS Hall of Fame.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bthsalumni.org/dr-lawrence-sirovich-51/|title=Dr. Lawrence Sirovich '51|work=BTHS Alumni Hall of Fame|publisher=Brooklyn Tech Alumni Foundation|access-date=2026-01-02}}</ref> Sirovich attended [[Johns Hopkins University]] as an undergraduate math major, and as a graduate student in aeronautical engineering (where applied mathematics was practiced).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/applied-mathematics/lawrence-sirovich|title=Lawrence Sirovich {{!}} Division of Applied Mathematics|website=www.brown.edu|access-date=2019-10-04}}</ref> In 1958, jointly with Johns Hopkins University, he became a research assistant at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute at NYU]]. It was there that he wrote his PhD dissertation "On the Kinetic Theory of Steady Gas Flows" in 1960.<ref>{{Cite book|title=On the kinetic theory of steady gas flows.|last=Sirovich, Lawrence.|date=1960|publisher=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University|oclc=1050245464}}</ref>  At the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]], [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs|K.O. Friedrichs]], a mathematician of great insight and taste, was his most influential teacher. For Sirovich, taking a course with [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs|Friedrichs]] on [[asymptotics]] was a life-changing experience. Another early mentor at the Courant Institute was [[Fritz John]], a mathematician of the highest character with whom Sirovich later started the eminent Applied Mathematical Sciences series, of [[Springer Verlag|Springer-Verlag Publishing]].

== Research ==
Sirovich's early research was in [[Kinetic theory of gases|kinetic theory]], its connection with [[fluid mechanics]], and such areas of fluid mechanics as [[supersonic flow]] and [[turbulence]]. A turning point in Sirovich's research came with his reading of Jim Watson's ''[[The Double Helix]]'', which caused Sirovich to realize that he was not engaged in the heroic research of his time. This prompted participation in a [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory|Cold Spring Harbor]] summer course on biology, and eventually led to his close association with [[Haldan Keffer Hartline|H. Keffer Hartline's]] Laboratory of Biophysics at the [[Rockefeller University]], and a long collaboration with Bruce W. Knight, the present head of the laboratory. As a maturing scientist, Sirovich's research interests took on an element of serendipity ("chance confers an advantage on the prepared mind", [[Louis Pasteur]]). For example, a chance remark on the failure of the standard description of the [[horseshoe crab]]'s lateral eye [[neural network]] at its boundaries led to a [[Wiener–Hopf method|Wiener-Hopf]] solution to the problem, with complete experimental agreement.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sirovich|first1=L.|last2=Brodie|first2=S.E.|last3=Knight|first3=B.W.|date=1979|title=Effect of boundaries on the response of a neural network|journal=Biophysical Journal|volume=28|issue=3|pages=423–445|doi=10.1016/s0006-3495(79)85191-7|pmid=262559|pmc=1328648|issn=0006-3495|bibcode=1979BpJ....28..423S}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Mach bands: quantitative studies on neural networks in the retina|last=Ratliff, Floyd.|date=1965|publisher=Holden-Day|oclc=1025246032}}</ref> An article by [[Linda Greenhouse]] in the ''[[New York Times]]'' led to "A pattern analysis of the second Rehnquist U.S. Supreme Court."<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Sirovich|first=Lawrence|date=2003-06-24|title=A pattern analysis of the second Rehnquist U.S. Supreme Court|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=100|issue=13|pages=7432–7437|doi=10.1073/pnas.1132164100|issn=0027-8424|pmc=164603|pmid=12821777|bibcode=2003PNAS..100.7432S|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/10/06/weekinreview/the-nation-the-court-same-time-next-year-and-next-year.html|title=The Nation; The Court: Same Time Next Year. And Next Year.|last=Greenhouse|first=Linda|date=2002-10-06|work=The New York Times|access-date=2019-10-04|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> An observation that human faces, are always different, but are always recognizable as a face; and likewise that images of turbulence had the same property of being different, and being recognizable as turbulence led to a successful model of [[Facial recognition system|face recognition]], and also served as an analysis model for turbulence. The former led to Sirovich's establishing the subject of [[face recognition]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Sirovich|first1=L.|last2=Kirby|first2=M.|date=1987-03-01|title=Low-dimensional procedure for the characterization of human faces|journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America A|volume=4|issue=3|pages=519–24|doi=10.1364/josaa.4.000519|pmid=3572578|issn=1084-7529|bibcode=1987JOSAA...4..519S|s2cid=982857}}</ref> Allied to this was the notion of low dimensional dynamical descriptions of turbulence in standard geometrical settings.  In a series of three papers on the subject, Sirovich established the field of low dimensional dynamical models.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Sirovich|first=Lawrence|date=1987-10-01|title=Turbulence and the dynamics of coherent structures. I. Coherent structures|journal=Quarterly of Applied Mathematics|volume=45|issue=3|pages=561–571|doi=10.1090/qam/910462|issn=0033-569X|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Sirovich|first=Lawrence|date=1987-10-01|title=Turbulence and the dynamics of coherent structures. III. Dynamics and scaling|journal=Quarterly of Applied Mathematics|volume=45|issue=3|pages=583–590|doi=10.1090/qam/910464|issn=0033-569X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Sirovich met Carole Hochman, a number theorist, at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]]. Their first date took place on September 4, 1960, and they married October 16th, 1960.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.myheritage.com/names/lawrence_sirovich|title=Lawrence Sirovich - Historical Records|website=www.myheritage.com|access-date=2019-10-07}}</ref> Carole received her PhD from the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]] and later became Chair of the Department of Math and Science at the Pratt Institute, which she retired from in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pratt.edu/faculty_and_staff/bio/?id=csirovic|title=Pratt Institute|website=www.pratt.edu|access-date=2019-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=33471|title=Carole Sirovich - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2019-10-04}}</ref>

Their daughter Brenda Sirovich was born in 1963, and received a B.A. in math and biology from [[Harvard University|Harvard]]. She is the co-director of the VA Outcomes Group at [[Geisel School of Medicine|Dartmouth's Geisel School of Medicine]].  Their son Matthew was born in 1966. Matt studied math and economics at [[Brown University]], and is currently a board member there.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/about/administration/corporation/members/matthew-i-sirovich|title=Matthew I. Sirovich {{!}} The Corporation of Brown University|website=www.brown.edu|access-date=2019-10-04}}</ref>

In 2018 Mathew Sirovich honored his parents by endowing the Carole & Lawrence Sirovich Chair of Public Health at [[Brown University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brown.edu/news/2018-01-04/professorships|title=Investment in endowed professorships brings top talent to Brown|website=Brown University|language=en|access-date=2019-10-04}}</ref>
